newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: EU Cognac, whisky producers to benefit from ITA.
newsitem.headline: EU Cognac, whisky producers to benefit from ITA.

text.p: European Union producers of whisky, cognac and other distilled spirits will be direct beneficiaries of the information technology agreement sealed on Thursday between the EU and the United States.

EU trade commissioner Sir Leon Brittan told a news conference that, in conjunction with the accord, tariffs on brown distilled spirits traded between the EU and the United States will be eliminated by the year 2000.
Tariffs on white spirts and liqueurs will be removed over five years, he added.

"We have made it clear for several months that it would greatly help our ability to reach an ITA if the product coverage could be as wide as possible -- both within ITA products and better still beyond IT products," Peter Guilford, Brittan's spokesman, told reporters.
"We're not trying to pretend that whisky and cognac are IT products. We're saying, merely, the more the merrier. We believe in cutting tariffs where you can," he said.
EU officials estimated the duties to be removed at 27 million ECUs a year.
Brittan announced earlier on Thursday the 15 member European Union Council of trade ministers endorsed an agreement with the U.S. on a global information technology pact.
Trade officials said including tariff cuts on spirits was in large part a sweetener to help persuade France to put aside its reservations about the ITA.

"We are opening our market in a serious way in semi-conductors and we think it is more balanced and more ambitious if we can broaden coverage not only in IT products, which we have now successfully done, but also in some non-IT products," he added.
The EU spokesman said he hoped clinching an ITA would also give a boost to talks aimed at freeing up telecommunications services, which are due to conclude by February 15.

"We happen to believe it will give a spur to encourage countries to be generous in their offers on telecommunications, which is the other big harvest that we're looking for in concrete terms at this session in Singapore," he added.
